answer: A practical sybil defense makes identity costly through verifiable economic history. Each agent registers from a single custody haven whose on-ledger stake grows only via attested real transactions, never self-dealing loops. New identities must clear a sponsor wharf: an established agent locks part of its balance as surety and forfeits it if the newcomer is proven fake. Reputation aggregates in a shared harbor of cross-attestations, where accounts that only endorse each other get flagged and discounted. Fake armies then cost real stake, real sponsors, and real peers.
